## Summary

White-Rodgers is a thermostat and controls brand whose history page,
published by Copeland, credits it with the first White-Rodgers
programmable thermostat and the Sensi smart thermostats, and records
its move to the Emerson campus and its merger with Emerson Flow
Controls [2]. Copeland, headquartered in St. Louis, was acquired by
Emerson in 1986 and returned to stand-alone status in 2023, with White
Rodgers and Sensi among its brands [3]. The IEEE registry lists one
MA-L block to White Rodgers Division at 8100 West Florissant, St.
Louis [1].

A MAC in this block is most likely a Sensi Wi-Fi thermostat. Sensi's
router-compatibility page says the 1F86U-42WF and UP500W thermostats
come in Murata-radio and Qualcomm-radio versions and require IEEE power
save polling [4]; it gives neither the Wi-Fi generation nor the band.

The founding year, the exact radio silicon, MAC randomization and any
security advisory are not documented by the sources consulted. FCC
grantee codes are not listed: the FCC ID databases refused the session
that verified this entry, and nothing is filled in from memory.
